posts.title: 13,000 raw records → 12,000+ scored leads
posts.tip: X thread (6 posts): hook → problem → clean → score → write → lesson + link in reply.

captions.label: LinkedIn / Facebook
captions.text:
13,000 raw records. 12,000+ scored leads.

A client came to us with a huge prospect list and one problem: nobody could tell who to call first, and every message sounded the same.

So we built a lead engine:
1. Clean: removed duplicates, fixed broken fields, filled the gaps
2. Score: ranked every lead on how well they fit and how ready they look
3. Write: an AI audit engine drafted a tailored opening line for each prospect

The team now starts every day with a ranked list and a personal hook for each call.
A human still approves every message. That part stays human.

The lesson: your old list is probably worth more than you think. It just needs a system.

Want us to look at yours? Link in the first comment.
#LeadGeneration #AIAutomation #CRM #Eaglescroft

posts.title: Edit faster without cutting corners: our AI-assisted video workflow
posts.tip: Facebook and X: post the 6 slides as a carousel. LinkedIn: upload the PDF as a document post (title: "Edit faster without cutting corners").

captions.label: LinkedIn / Facebook
captions.text:
Video is the most-watched format on every platform, and the most time-hungry to make.

Here's the AI-assisted workflow we use at Eaglescroft:
→ Script: AI drafts from a brief, we rewrite the first 3 seconds by hand
→ Voice: clean-up or AI voice, depending on the brief
→ Rough cut: automatic captions and silence removal
→ Polish: B-roll, motion and branding, still done by a human editor

AI does the heavy lifting. Taste is still human.
Which step eats most of your time? Comment 1, 2, 3 or 4 👇
#VideoEditing #AIVideo #ContentCreation #Eaglescroft

posts.title: GoHighLevel's AI Employee: what it does, costs and who should skip it
posts.tip: Re-check HighLevel's current AI Employee pricing and language support before this goes out.

captions.label: LinkedIn / Facebook
captions.text:
Your CRM can now answer your phone. Should it?

GoHighLevel's "AI Employee" bundles AI for chat and SMS, phone calls, review replies and content into one add-on.

Our honest take, from auditing HighLevel builds:
Good fit: your leads already live in HighLevel and you miss calls after hours.
Check first: the real monthly cost. The add-on is billed per sub-account, on top of your plan.
Check first: language support for your customers before promising voice AI.
Skip it: if your follow-up process is broken. AI will only automate the mess.

Fix the process first, then switch on the AI.
#GoHighLevel #CRM #AIAutomation #MarketingAutomation

posts.title: Don't ask AI if your idea is good. Ask how it fails.
posts.tip: X: the prompt as a single post plus the graphic.

captions.label: LinkedIn / Facebook
captions.text:
Don't ask AI if your idea is good. It will usually say yes.

Ask it how your idea fails.

The prompt we use before every big decision at Eaglescroft:
"Here's my plan: [paste plan]. Act as a sceptical investor. Give me the 3 strongest reasons it could fail, and what would prove each one wrong."

Then a human decides. Every time.
Save this for your next planning meeting.
#PracticalAI #PromptEngineering #Eaglescroft

posts.title: Before you plug AI into your business, ask these 5 questions

captions.label: LinkedIn / Facebook
captions.text:
Before you plug AI into your business, ask these 5 questions:
1. Who can see our data?
2. Is it stored, or used to train the model?
3. Is every action logged?
4. Who is accountable when it's wrong?
5. Can we switch it off tomorrow?

If a vendor can't answer all five clearly, wait.
Save this for your next software demo.
#AIGovernance #DataPrivacy #AIForBusiness #Eaglescroft

posts.title: AI for a literature review, without cheating
posts.tip: LinkedIn: upload the PDF as a document post (title: "AI for your literature review, without cheating"). X: post slides 1, 4 and 5 with the X caption.

captions.label: LinkedIn
captions.text:
Lecturers and students keep asking me the same question: "Is using AI for research cheating?"

It depends on how you use it. Here's the line I'd draw:
✓ Finding papers faster: fine
✓ Summarising so you know what to read properly: fine
✓ Critiquing your draft: fine
✗ Copying its citations without checking: dangerous, because AI invents references
✗ Letting it write your argument: that's not your work any more

Use AI to research faster, not to think less. Check your institution's policy and be open about how you used it.
Academics: what rules is your department setting? I'd love to hear.

posts.title: The 1-page AI policy every small company needs

captions.label: LinkedIn
captions.text:
Your team is already using AI. The question is whether they're using it safely.

Every small company needs a 1-page AI policy. It only needs 4 parts:
1. Approved tools and approved uses
2. What never goes into public AI tools (customer data, passwords, confidential files)
3. A human checks anything that goes to a customer
4. One person owns AI questions, and the policy is reviewed every quarter

One page beats no page. Save this and share it with whoever runs your operations.
